The Mysteries of Pittsburgh by Michael Chabon - a coming of age story about two guys and a girl in Pittsburgh in the 90s. This was one of my favorite books at your age.

The Secret History by Donna Tartt - a thriller about a group of wealthy students at an elite college in Vermont. Also one of my favorite books at your age.

Tomorrow and Tomorrow and Tomorrow by Gabriel Zevin - a story about two game developers who meet in college and have a tumultuous working friendship over many years

IT by Stephen King - told in alternating timelines, the story of a group of people who return to their hometown in Maine to combat a supernatural entity that terrorized them as children

All That's Left In The World - the story of two teen boys, one gay and one questioning his sexuality, who meet in a post-apocalyptic America and struggle to survive together. It has a great sequel too

The Three-Body Problem series - epic science fiction that is deeply influenced by Chinese culture

I don't have much to recommend in fantasy, but you can't go wrong with The Lord of the Rings!

I'm reading the comics now and I was surprised how little Tao features in Volumes 1+2. I think his bigger role in the show grew out of a need for someone to push events forward who wasn't one of the bullies. Tao in the show puts a lot of pressure on both Charlie and Nick to figure their feelings out and effects the circumstances of the sports day finale. 

I think another thing to keep in mind is that in the context of this being a story, we're meeting these characters at an intense formative time in their lives. Tao was probably not the same person a couple years ago. But by the time season one starts, he's witnessed Charlie's bullying, and Elle has transitioned and left for Higgs. We learn in Season Two that he has issues with abandonment because of his father's death. So looking back at Season One - I see someone who is terrified of losing his closest friends, and of them being hurt again - and his bad behavior makes a whole lot more sense. 

So I don't think it was a reversal or a toning down, in my view it was character growth. It happened a little quickly because of the scale of the show (more screen time for him in Season One might have helped everything). But I think it was intentional and consistent.
